than re-finding it.

| concurrent execution | run A writing while run B's compensation unlinks | covered as accepted scope boundary R-2 (probe 26b P12) — standing; no invariant promised |

## 3. Findings

### F-01 [P1|partial-failure/uncontracted-state|needs-user:false]

- section/artifact: spec/11-spec-v11.md §4.5 Error paths (lines 766-771),
  §5.1 diagram WRITE_OUTPUT edges (lines 840-842), §4.5 mutation rows
  3/6/10 (lines 782/785/789), §7.1 E-MEM row, §7.2 footprint sentence,
  QC-2 (Scope line 1470), §8.3 T-C16 (line 1370), §12 glossary
  "successful open" row; decision register D-46/D-54/R-5/R-6.
- claim or missing contract: the spec's failure taxonomy partitions the
  open boundary into exactly two contracted classes — at-open **OSError**
  (D-46: report directly, target byte-untouched) and at-open **KI**
  (D-54/R-6: fd never binds, no compensation, 0-byte residue recorded).
  The third member of the same window — an at-open **MemoryError** — has
  no classification, no state contract, and no risk record anywhere.
- evidence (live, 48b P2a/P2b): the kernel applies O_CREAT|O_TRUNC inside
  `open()`; the CPython wrapper then fails to allocate (MemoryError)
  before `fd` is bound; the raw fd is closed by the wrapper's cleanup, the
  created/truncated inode remains. The §4.5 reference shape observes
  `fd is None` → no compensation → the run reports
  `csv2json: error: out of memory writing <out>` (E-MEM **write-phase**
  form, exit 1) while the target is left PRESENT at 0 bytes — absent
  target CREATED (P2a: state=(True, 0)), pre-existing target TRUNCATED
  (P2b: 440-byte prior → 0). Probe:
  `python3 appendix/48b-adv-c11-probes.py` → P2a/P2b/P2c all reproduce.
- minimal counterexample: (1) absent target `out.json`; (2) valid input;
  (3) MemoryError strikes the open wrapper's allocation after the kernel
  applied O_CREAT|O_TRUNC; (4) run exits 1 with
  `out of memory writing out.json`; (5) `out.json` exists, 0 bytes.
  §4.5 Error paths says an at-open failure "reports directly with NO
  compensation (target byte-untouched)" — for this class the target is
  NOT byte-untouched (0-byte created). §5.1's pre-open MemoryError edge
  says "filesystem untouched" — false here. T-C16 says for the write-phase
  form "the correct assertion is that the path is ABSENT ... no conforming
  mechanism can otherwise leave it present" — a conforming reference-shape
  run (48b P2) left it PRESENT at exactly that phase form. The contracts
  cannot all hold for this window.
- impact: T-C16's write-phase assertion fails on the conforming shape;
  the state taxonomy (§4.5 rows 3/6/10, §7.2) is incomplete for a window
  D-54 itself proves is reachable; a cold implementor has no rule for the
  state and cannot decide whether to compensate.
- required disposition: classify at-open MemoryError. Either (a) fold it
  into the D-54 at-open class by its observable (fd is None → no
  compensation → the same two-flavor 0-byte residue, widening R-6's
  trigger from "KI" to "KI or MemoryError at open"), plus a §5.1 edge and
  a T-C16 qualifier mirroring the R-5/R-6 exception shape; or (b) contract
  a D-33 trigger for it explicitly. The spec must also reconcile T-C16's
  "no conforming mechanism can otherwise leave it present" sentence with
  whichever class is chosen. Note the symmetry argument the fix can lean
  on: D-54's own rationale (fd-binding is the only observable boundary)
  applies verbatim to MemoryError.
- decision owner: spec-designer (mechanism-level classification; no
  product trade-off — the residue already has a recorded class for KI).
- verification required: adv-early or full adv-review re-run after the
  fix; T-C16's wording must be checked against the new classification
  (mechval keyword check unaffected).

### F-02 [P2|boundary-input|needs-user:false]

- section/artifact: spec/11-spec-v11.md §4.3.3 FSM table + normative
  counting rule (lines 436-458); §4.3.2 loop (lines 380-431); QC-5
  Mechanism (line 1561); NFR-003 (§9, T-C9).
- claim: the spec mandates two independent full passes over every record's
  span — the FSM scan "with states FIELD_START/UNQUOTED/QUOTED/CLOSED"
  carrying its own record-relative counter (§4.3.3), and count_line_breaks
  over the same span (§4.3.2, `line += count_line_breaks(text, start,
  end)`), each pinned as a distinct mechanism with its own normative
  wording ("the two can never diverge" is achieved by duplicated
  arithmetic, not shared computation).
- evidence (live, 48c): the literal §4.3.2+§4.3.3 walk over a 55 MB /
  250k-row input takes **27.3 s** on this Raspberry Pi 5 host — of the 30
  s NFR-003/T-C9 envelope — while the reader-only baseline is 0.8 s
  (34x). On the pinned shape the envelope is consumed by the mandated
  double scan alone, before serialize/write.
- minimal counterexample: (1) 50 MB / 250k-row input (the NFR-003
  envelope's own numbers); (2) a conforming implementation walks each
  record span twice per §4.3.2+§4.3.3; (3) on Pi-class hardware the walk
  alone is 27.3 s; (4) T-C9's "< 30 s" assertion now depends on untested
  interpreter margins (dict build, serialize, write, GC), and QC-5's
  "constant number of times" claim (line 1561: "one O(record) FSM scan +
  one O(record) break count") names exactly the two passes whose sum
  violates the envelope it certifies.
- impact: T-C9 flaps on the documented floor hardware class; the spec's
  own QC-5 Mechanism sentence certifies the cost structure that breaks
  its own Scope.
- required disposition: not a correctness defect — the counting is right
  (SR1-F-01's collapse rule verified again this cycle). Either relax
  T-C9/QC-5's host assumption explicitly (name the reference hardware
  class for the 30 s figure), or drop the double-scan mandate by wording
  §4.3.2/§4.3.3 to permit a single fused scan (the FSM already counts
  every terminator; `count_line_breaks` re-derives what the FSM's counter
  already computed — one conforming shape computes it once). No behavior
  change; wording only.
- decision owner: spec-designer.
- verification required: none blocking (P2); mechval keyword check on any
  edited claim sentence.

### F-03 [P2|test-premise|needs-user:false]

- section/artifact: spec/11-spec-v11.md §8.3 T-C8 (line 1362); §8.4 first
  bullet; §7.1 E-WRITE row.
- claim: T-C8's "non-writable dir → E-WRITE, no file created" sub-case
  carries no skip-as-root note, while the adjacent read-only-target
  sub-case does ("SKIP AS ROOT — DAC_OVERRIDE defeats mode 444").
- evidence (live, 48b P4a control + mechanism): as non-root (euid 1000)
  creating in a 0555 dir fails as expected (control). As root, CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE
  (and CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH) lets open(O_CREAT) in a 0555 dir SUCCEED — the
  at-open EACCES premise never materializes; the run proceeds to write.
  The same mechanism T-C2/T-C8 already document for mode-444 files
  applies verbatim to mode-0555 directories.
- minimal counterexample: (1) CI container runs as root (common default);
  (2) T-C8 sub-case sets dir mode 0555; (3) the tool's open succeeds via
  DAC_OVERRIDE; (4) the sub-case's expected E-WRITE never occurs and the
  assertion fails — or worse, a tester "fixes" it by asserting success,
  silently de-testing the at-open path.
- impact: environment-dependent test failure whose cause is the premise,
  not the tool; mirrors adv-c6 F-04's class exactly.
- required disposition: add "SKIP AS ROOT (DAC_OVERRIDE defeats mode 0555
  dirs, T-C2's convention)" to the non-writable-dir sub-case — one-line
  edit mirroring the existing convention two clauses earlier in the same
  row.
- decision owner: spec-designer.
- verification required: none (P2); the note parallels existing text.

### F-04 [P3|editorial|needs-user:false]

- section/artifact: spec/11-spec-v11.md §5.1 diagram, WRITE_OUTPUT edges

- claim: the pre-open MemoryError edge reads "MemoryError(pre-open encode:
  nothing open — filesystem untouched)" — accurate for the encode step,
  but the same edge label style ("at-open OSError edge: NO compensation")
  omits the at-open MemoryError class entirely (F-01's textual shadow).
- evidence: grep — §5.1 has no MemoryError-at-open edge; §4.5 Error paths
  sentence "an at-open failure reports directly with NO compensation
  (target byte-untouched)" is the only at-open phrasing and it inherits
  F-01's uncontracted state.
- minimal counterexample: n/a (mechanical gap; the F-01 counterexample is
  the operative one).
- impact: editorial only once F-01 is dispositioned; kept separate so the
  F-01 fix doesn't miss the diagram.
- required disposition: whatever F-01 chooses, add the corresponding §5.1
  edge (or fold into F-01's fix).
- decision owner: spec-designer.
- verification required: with F-01's gate.
